AI Makes Research Faster, but Is It Killing Serendipity?
> Jonah argues that AI makes research faster and better but removes the accidental discoveries that came from browsing dictionaries, libraries, and web links.
> “AI one-shots the research, the same way looking up a word online does. You don't need to search around, so you rarely stumble onto adjacent ideas.”
Source:
https://x.com/jonah_b/status/2110891773921046586

tweet.text:
AI has made my research better. But I realized today it’s also costing me something...

When I was in middle school, I asked my grandpa what a word meant. He told me to go grab the dictionary and look it up. I asked why I couldn’t just look it up online. He said that would get me the answer for sure, but I’d be missing something. When you open a dictionary, you see all the words next to the one you’re looking up, and you end up learning a few of those too. Looking it up online gets you the one word and nothing around it. No serendipity.

Zooming out, the internet era already lost some of that serendipity. It used to be that for a research project, you had to go find a book in the library. On the way to that book, you’d see books you’d never heard of. And while you were looking through its table of contents for the information you needed, you’d inevitably pick up other concepts too.

Internet research is much more directed. What you’re trading is access to more information, faster, but
